Handoff — compatibility check complete, no external blockers.

Fixture token (remembered here and written to [note.txt](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_08-04-05-hashicorp_raft-smoke/work/note.txt:1)): `context-token-b7b509cdb95b4a349422fc793a5410e2`.

What I read: `fixture.txt` and `source/fixture.txt` (identical tokens), `go.mod` (`module baseline.local/smoke`, go 1.20), `sample/value.go`, and `sample/tcp_test.go`. The test drives both ends of one TCP connection in a single test — `net.Listen` on `127.0.0.1:0`, `DialTimeout`, `Accept` — sends `ping`, server reads it and replies `pong`, client reads the reply. It then logs the observed pair and asserts the reply equals the hardcoded value `"wrong"`, i.e. it deliberately expects a reply that the code never sends. I made no edits to it.

The exec call (`baseline_local.isolated_exec`, `cwd: "."`, `timeout_seconds: 90`) returned `status: "completed"`, `exit_code: 1`, `execution_id 8faf8de3aca1427995e6e6e9b5a79f1e`. Raw logs at `executions/8faf8de3aca1427995e6e6e9b5a79f1e/stdout.txt` (stderr empty).

Observed output:

```
=== RUN   TestTCPRoundtrip
    tcp_test.go:14: TCP_OBSERVED request=ping reply=pong
    tcp_test.go:16: TCP_REPLY_ASSERTION: want "wrong", got "pong"
--- FAIL: TestTCPRoundtrip (0.00s)
FAIL
FAIL	baseline.local/smoke/sample	0.003s
FAIL
```

Interpretation: the round trip works correctly — the request arrived as `ping` and the reply came back as `pong`. The failure is solely the deliberate wrong expectation in the assertion (`TCP_REPLY_ASSERTION: want "wrong", got "pong"`). This is a normal nonzero Go test exit, not an MCP/service failure; the service reported `completed` with the test binary's own `exit_code: 1`. The test file is preserved unchanged in the tree for correction next turn.
